items.title: Morning Digest: Trump says U.S. military action against Iran not necessary ‘at this point’; U.K. writer M. John Harrison wins Booker for AI-tinged apocalyptic novel, and more - The Hindu
items.excerpt: Published - November 10, 2026 06:24 am IST ... #### Trump says U.S. military action against Iran not necessary ‘at this point’ U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday (November 9, 2026) told reporters he believes the war in Iran “militarily is effectively over.” The President made a surprise visit to the White House briefing room after meeting with Qatar’s Prime Minister earlier in the day. “Iran militarily is effectively over,” Mr. Trump said. “We’re just keeping it the status quo.” #### U.K. writer M. John Harrison wins Booker for AI-tinged apocalyptic novel U.K. author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday (November 9, 2026) for his enigmatic novel “The End of Everything”, which echoes concerns about artificial intelligence in a darkly satirical depiction of post-apocalyptic Britain. Mr. Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize and a boost in sales and profile for the winner. #### At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi Air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with experts warning that the gaps have led to understated pollution levels and resulted in a lower official air quality index (AQI). According to Dr. D. Saha, former head of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)’s air quality laboratory, AQI values are calculated using a moving or running average of hourly concentrations of eight parameters, including PM2.5 and PM10, over the previous 24 hours. #### Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov India is ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish “food corridors”, announced Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcoming the offer after a telephone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of the Ukraine-Russia peace talks set to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Mr. Modi conveyed India’s “readiness” to help with all initiatives to end the nearly five-year-old conflict. The call was followed by another call between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv. ... #### Trump says likely to meet Putin, Xi at China APEC summit United States President Donald Trump has said he will likely meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in a rare trilateral leaders’ meeting on the sidelines of the APEC gathering in Shenzhen next week. Beijing said on Monday (November 9, 2026) it was “in communication with relevant parties” over the meeting, not ruling out the possibility as leaders gather for the APEC summit in southern China on November 18 and 19. #### Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinised after foreign intelligence concerns U.S. President Donald Trump’s close relationship with embattled ‌Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday (November 9, 2026), after the company ​said its board was investigating whether the tech executive has been the target ⁠of a foreign intelligence effort. Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates to at least 2025. Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support ‌for the administration’s agenda and become a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market. #### Hegseth faces expected U.S. House impeachment vote this week Pete Hegseth, the U.S. Defence Secretary, calls himself the Secretary of War, part of his effort to rebrand ‌a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year. Now, with ​a House impeachment vote expected this week, he could soon share something in common with an ⁠actual secretary of war. U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday (November 9, 2026), setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power. #### Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to more than a decade in prison British comedian and Hollywood star Russell Brand was sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault by the Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday (November 9, 2026). Brand, 51, was found guilty on Thursday (November 5, 2026) by the court of rape and three counts of sexual assault and not guilty on three other counts. He was charged in relation to a total of seven crimes. His crimes were committed between 2004 and 2009. ... Brand has the possibility of being released in about seven years subject to conditions, the judge said.

items.title: A key report for where inflation stood in October comes out Tuesday. Here's what to expect
items.excerpt: Published Mon, Nov 9 2026 4:03 PM EST Jeff Cox@jeff.cox.7528@JeffCoxCNBCcom Key Points - The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release the October consumer price index report Tuesday, with estimates of a 0.3% headline growth rate and 0.2% for core. - While the report won't include an annual rate because of last year's government shutdown, the results likely will keep the Fed well above its 2% inflation goal. - "We've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday. ... Falling gasoline prices provided some relief to consumers in October, but Federal Reserve officials are increasingly concerned that inflation pressures elsewhere in the economy are proving harder to contain. Prices at the pump declined by more than 4%, according to the Energy Information Administration, providing a respite from a surge that had added more than a dollar a gallon over the past year. However, the consumer price index for the month, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release Tuesday at 8:30 a.m., is expected to show only a slight let-up. Meanwhile, Fed officials say they are worried that inflation initially driven higher by President Donald Trump's tariffs and the Iran war is proving more persistent than expected, with price pressures emerging in sectors beyond those directly affected by the shocks. At a time when the central bank is increasingly confident about the state of the labor market, concerns over the cost of living are what are top of mind for the Fed. "We've been moving up to what historically we'd consider full employment, and the big problem has all been on the inflation side. We go around, we talk to people everywhere in this district, all we hear about is affordability on the business side, the cost," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday during an event in his home district. "So we've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure." The CPI reading for all items is expected to show an increase of 0.3%. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, is forecast to increase 0.2%, according to the Dow Jones consensus forecast. While both would be slower than the respective September monthly gains of 0.6% and 0.3%, they still represent further price pressures. There will be no annual reading for October because of the government shutdown a year ago, which prevented the BLS from collecting some data and compiling a full index level. Because of the data issue, there isn't a comparable figure for the index. Bank of America, using an assumed baseline interpolating data for the period last year, estimated the annual growth rates at 3.8% for headline and 2.7% for core, both 0.1 percentage point higher than September and well above the Fed's 2% goal. Goolsbee said the current run on inflation is defying what normally could be expected from supply shocks and tariffs, with the current situation intensified by the hyperscaler build-out related to artificial intelligence. "It was supposed to have gone away by now, and we're now starting to see the inflation kicking up in areas that probably weren't from oil prices and tariffs, like a bunch of services. Now this stuff with the AI data center build-out is, to my eyes, starting to look more just like old-fashioned demand overheating," he said. The massive investment in data centers is creating demand for construction workers, electricity and equipment, potentially adding to price pressures even as AI promises longer-term productivity gains, he added. ## Pressure on rates Though the Fed in October voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in place, markets are pricing in a better than 80% probability that the central bank will raise rates by a quarter percentage point at its next meeting in December, according to CME FedWatch data. Goolsbee, who doesn't vote on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year but will in 2027, didn't commit to which way he was leaning on additional rate hikes, though he said current conditions could warrant action. "The conventional wisdom there is: Be aggressive up front, to never let the economy overheat, because once it gets overheated, it's extremely painful to get rid of that kind of overheating," he said. "So I think we've got to watch out in that space." The CPI release comes with economic growth strong — 3.4% in the third quarter for gross domestic product and tracking at 3.5% for the final three months of the year, according to the Atlanta Fed — and the labor market seemingly in solid shape as well. Nonfarm payrolls expanded by a much better-than-expected 165,000 in October, while the unemployment rate edged lower to 4.1%, though inflation-adjusted wage growth has been negative. That puts the inflation reading squarely in focus. Bank of America said it sees tariff impacts fading but that goods prices could be pushed higher because of AI demand. Further, the firm is cautious about "sticky" services prices as well as pressures from health insurance and autos. The bank has been hawkish in terms of Fed expectations and sees a December hike as likely so long as there isn't an escalated stock market sell-off that might dissuade the central bank. "This will be the final inflation report before the Fed's December 8-9 meeting. If our forecast is correct, we think it would effectively lock in another 25bp hike, all else equal," BofA economist Stephen Juneau said in a client note. "Absent an indisputably soft 0.1% [month-over-month] print, we doubt the inflation data will dissuade the Fed from hiking in December. The bigger risk to our call comes from financial markets."

items.title: BLS will omit 12-month CPI, Core CPI figures from October report By Investing.com
items.excerpt: Published Nov 10, 2026, 03:32 AM Updated Nov 10, 2026, 03:48 AM ... Investing.com -- The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release its consumer price index report for October on Tuesday without the standard 12-month percentage change figures. The missing data stems from the 2025 government shutdown, which prevented BLS from collecting portions of price data for October 2025. The agency was unable to obtain that information retroactively, according to BLS spokesperson Cody Parkinson. The CPI report typically shows price changes compared to both the previous month and the prior year. The 12-month figure, which was 3.7% in September, is generally how the public understands inflation. Without the October 2025 data, BLS cannot calculate the 12-month percentage change for either the overall CPI or the core measure that excludes food and energy prices. Real earnings growth from a year earlier, a separate but related release, will also be unavailable. The report will still include month-over-month comparisons. Economists expect the CPI rose 0.3% in October from the previous month, while core CPI increased 0.2%.

items.title: US inflation set to slow after two months of cost pressures | The Star
items.excerpt: Tuesday, 10 Nov 2026 WASHINGTON: Prices for US goods and services have probably risen at a slower pace after two particularly uncomfortable months for American consumers. The consumer price index (CPI) for October was seen rising 0.3% after a 0.6% increase that was the largest since April, based on the median projection in a Bloomberg survey of economists ahead of today’s Bureau of Labour Statistics’ release. The core measure, which excludes often-volatile energy and food components, also probably cooled. The survey median sees a 0.2% increase for October, which would be the smallest advance in three months. The agency won’t publish year-on-year figures after it skipped the October 2025 CPI release due to the federal government shutdown at the time. The October CPI will be the last before the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) meeting in December, at which investors expect policymakers to boost interest rates. Economists will assess the finer details of the report for clues on inflation risks into early 2027. Economists at Citigroup Inc said in a recent note that they anticipate limited pass-through of high energy costs to goods prices, as well as moderate services inflation. “We expect headline CPI slowed to 0.25% in October (versus 0.65% prior). The core likely softened to 0.24% (versus 0.33% prior), with both softer goods and services price gains driving the improvement. “For goods, used cars and consumer electronics – categories that have faced pressure from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom – saw slower inflation. For services, gains in owners’ equivalent rent are down a third from a September spike,” said Bloomberg Economics. The latest snapshot of inflation also follows last Friday’s stronger-than-expected October jobs report. Sustained employment growth has the potential of ensuring consumers keep spending, while allowing the Fed to keep its focus squarely on inflation. Another price report, due on Friday, is projected to show nagging inflationary pressures faced by companies. The producer price index is forecast to accelerate to 6.6% for the year through October, the steepest annual increase in nearly four years.

Thomas Massie moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth based largely on the war in Iran. The impeachment resolution also includes references to Hegseth’s role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela. A vote in the House could come by mid-week. Hegseth said he would hold a press conference on Tuesday — his first in over 180 days — on the impeachment threat. He said the war was necessary, even if unpopular. Massie filed the impeachment resolution as soon as the House opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. Lawmakers are returning to Washington for just six short weeks — a lame-duck sprint to finish the Republican agenda before the GOP majorities end with the change of power on Jan. 3, 2027. ... ## Trump rejects amnesty for people living in the US illegally After suggesting he was open to negotiating a deal with Democrats on immigration policy that he acknowledged might have been too tough, Trump on Monday said an amnesty was off the table. “There won’t be amnesty,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “Somebody suggested, will there be amnesty? No, but— they came in. They knew the law.” Trump defended his administration’s deportation policy as “very strong.” Asked if he had talked with his newly promoted chief of staff, Stephen Miller, about immigration changes, Trump said no. “My policy hasn’t changed,” he said, adding that the focus will be on removing “the worst of the worst.” ## Trump says he’ll support Hegseth through impeachment attempt “I’ll stand by him,” President Trump told reporters Monday, hours after a congressman introduced an impeachment resolution for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. U.S. Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterm election. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth’s role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela, with Massie saying Hegseth “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.” On Monday, Trump commended Hegseth for having “won the war” in Venezuela and as “winning the war” in Iran, which continues to drag on. Trump went on to criticize Massie as a “sick guy” and a “loser.” Hegseth has set a rare press briefing for Tuesday to discuss the matter.

items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about the FBI looking into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent. ... The sudden emergence of Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence. ... China denied on Monday it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, saying the spying allegations were unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing. Huang has acknowledged he had been intimate with a business executive, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. He did not name the woman. Nvidia announced Sunday it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort." The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.

items.excerpt: November 9, 2026 | 7:05 pm ## We Are Imaginary releases music video FILIPINO indie-rock band We Are Imaginary has dropped the official music video for “Are We There Yet?,” the latest single from their 2026 self-titled album. Directed by Jam Lasin of Cream Flower, the music video captures the band in their jamming element, stitching together performances, candid moments, and visual references that pay tribute to their 18-year career as an underground force in the Filipino independent music scene. The music video also traces the highs and lows of band life. The track, which retains the post-punk guitar sensibilities of its original demo, is available on all streaming platforms. ## 2 Valid IDs hits P100-million box office milestone POWERED by word of mouth and a growing audience campaign, the small independent film 2 Valid IDs starring Marietta Subong (a.k.a. Pokwang) and directed by Ma-an L. Asuncion-Dagñalan, has crossed the P100-million mark at the Philippine box office. It has become one of the highest-grossing films in Cinemalaya history. Now on its fourth week in cinemas, the film generated interest online for its relatable storyline. Written by Abet Pagdadaganan Raz, 2 Valid IDs follows Sylvia, a poor provincial farmer trying to secure financial assistance for her hospitalized husband, made difficult due to frustrating bureaucratic processes that require two valid government-issued IDs. At Cinemalaya 2026, it won three awards: Best Actress for Ms. Subong, the Special Jury Award, and the Audience Choice Award. ## The Lord of the Rings concert coming in 2027 FILM Concerts Philippines has revealed that they will be presenting The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring in Concert on March 4, 5, and 6, 2027, at The Theatre at Solaire, Parañaque City. As Peter Jackson’s acclaimed film plays on the big screen, Howard Shore’s Academy Award-winning score will be performed live by the 247-member ensemble of the Filharmonika Orchestra, the Philippine Madrigal Singers’ adult and boys’ choirs, and soloist Malena Rampi, under the baton of conductor Reuben Blundell. This will mark the largest ensemble Film Concerts Philippines has assembled to date. Since the film’s premiere in 2008, The Fellowship of the Ring in Concert has been performed by leading orchestras worldwide. Exclusive pre-sale access for Film Concerts Philippines community members is ongoing until Nov. 11, with public ticket sales beginning Nov. 20. ## Zoë Kravitz, John C. Reilly star in How to Rob a Bank THE upcoming film How to Rob a Bank kicks off with a gang of masked livestreaming bank robbers turning the FBI on its head. In the middle of the investigation is special agent John West, played by John C. Reilly, who forms an unlikely partnership with a software engineer on house arrest, played by Zoë Kravitz. Their combined skills are needed to take the viral criminals down. How to Rob A Bank also stars Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Christian Slater, and Pete Davidson. The film arrives in Philippine cinemas on Nov. 11. ## LEYO releases new EP FILIPINO singer-songwriter LEYO has reimagined the Filipino harana (serenade) with modern sensibilities in Akda sa Pag-alala, a six-track EP released under Sony Music Entertainment. Blending classic OPM, acoustic pop, and R&B, it is a personal collection shaped by affection, longing, vulnerability, and self-discovery. It balances guitar riffs and bass lines with jazzy, bossa nova-lite inflections, borrowing from a range of influences like The Beatles, Stevie Wonder, the APO Hiking Society, and the Manila Sound. The EP’s producers include 2026 Awit Awards winner Brian Lotho, Rain Santana, and LEYO himself. Akda sa Pag-alala is out now on all digital music platforms worldwide. ## George Michael concert film coming in Nov. GEORGE MICHAEL Entertainment, in partnership with Mercury Studios, has announced the start of the worldwide theatrical release of a brand-new, never-before-seen film titled George Michael: The Faith Tour, with screenings beginning on Nov. 11. Shot at the iconic Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour in 1988, the film captures a turning point that transformed George Michael from a global superstar into an era-defining artist. Directed by Andy Morahan and David Austin, this once-lost film has been restored and remastered, transforming archival footage assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm film into a cinematic experience. ... ## Dune, Dune: Part Two return for a limited time TO RELIVE the journey before experiencing the third and final installment of the film series this December, Dune and Dune: Part Two will be back in cinemas and IMAX for one week starting Nov. 11. items.title: Miranda Lambert Announces 'Songline' Album and Film
items.excerpt: Source: Billboard · November 10, 2026 Miranda Lambert has announced the release of her 'Songline' album and companion film, as reported by Billboard. The project commemorates her recent concert at The Truth, a new Nashville venue. The show features Lambert performing a mix of her hits and new music from Crisco, alongside her longtime band and a 12-piece orchestra. Songline includes performances of tracks such as “Bluebird,” “Crisco” and “Gunpowder & Lead.” In addition to performances from the show, the upcoming Songline film will feature interview footage from Lambert and many of her collaborators, including Frank Liddell, Jesse Frasure, Luke Dick and Natalie Hemby. A live version of “Snakeskin Boots” has been released on Amazon Music as a preview to the project. Lambert is heading into this year’s CMA Awards with seven nominations, including two in the musical event of the year category and one for female artist of the year.
